SCHOOL ROOM · THE CLUBS · 45 CARDS · AGES 3–12

The Clubs — every card opens a hobby.

Forty-five after-school clubs on forty-five cards: art, music, dance and thirteen more for the youngest members, then chess, coding, fencing and the rest for ages 6 and up. Every card prints the two skills its club trains — Aim & Focus, Calm & Wellbeing, Measure & Create — every club has its lesson and printable twin right here, and the room was built for choosing: try one, keep one, grow one.

Open the club shelves ↓The printable set ↗
HOW THIS ROOM WORKS

Pick a club. Read its skills. Try it this week.

Every card in this deck does two jobs: it names one club and it prints the two skills that club trains, right under the picture. The room splits by age the way the school does: the first shelf holds the fifteen clubs made for the youngest members — tagged Ages 3+ — and the second shelf holds the thirty clubs for older members, tagged Ages 6+. When one club becomes a favorite, its lesson page carries the full teaching — what the club is, what the skills secretly train, the parent script, the questions to ask — and the library page holds the printable twin with a download button.

A word on safety, because it matters here: some clubs are coach clubs. Fencing and archery always run with a trained coach and proper equipment — their pages say so — and swimming, climbing and horse riding belong wherever trained adults and the right gear are standard. The card starts the hobby; the grown-ups keep it safe.

THE YOUNG CLUB SHELF · AGES 3+

Fifteen clubs for the youngest members.

Art, music, dance, sports, drama, gardening, cooking, ballet, yoga, swimming, reading, crafts, drawing, baking and singing — the fifteen clubs that work from age three, in the order the school recommends trying them. Read every card right here on this page.

ArtMusicDanceSportsDramaGardeningCookingBalletYogaSwimmingReadingCraftsDrawingBakingSinging
THE OLDER CLUB SHELF · AGES 6+

Thirty clubs for ages 6 and up.

From archery to volunteering — the strategy clubs, the workshop clubs, the coach-led sports and the word clubs. Younger members wait for these; the skills are worth the wait.

ArcheryAstronomyBird WatchingCalligraphyChessChoirClimbingCodingCyclingDebateFencingFashion DesignFilmmakingFirst AidGymnasticsHorse RidingJournalingLegoMartial ArtsNature CraftsPhotographyPoetryPotteryPuppetryRoboticsScienceSkateboardingTable TennisTennisVolunteering
GAMES THE CLUBS PLAY

Warm-ups from the games shelf.

Club time and game time trade places all afternoon, and the school’s games shelf holds the rules for the warm-ups every club borrows: Animal Walks opens dance, drama and yoga bodies, Musical Statues trains the freeze every performance needs, Relay Race is sports club’s favorite drill, Obstacle Course is gymnastics night at home, and Simon Says sharpens the listening every club runs on. Full rules on every page.

AROUND THE SCHOOL

Where to wander next.

Explore the School — every room, one door each ↗The Growing-up classrooms on the Learning Path ↗Visit the Art Studio · ages 3–12 ↗Run an experiment in the Science Lab ↗Go outside with the Nature Club ↗

The Clubs sit on the school’s room shelf beside the Library, the Garden, the Playground, the Music Room and the Art Room — and they belong to the Growing-up classrooms the Learning Path points to: the Art Studio, the Science Lab and the Nature Club are the neighbors a new hobby grows into.

A hobby is a curriculum. Every card here hides real work — focus, patience, practice, courage — inside something the child thinks is just their club. Try the thing first; the skills follow the fun.

FLASHCARDS

Prefer printed cards?

The cards from this class also live in the flashcards library — every card is right there on the shelf with the picture, the words to say together and a download button, ready for away-from-screen time.
